title: Operatorless k8s bootstrap: vSphere + bare metal constraints and terraform notes
content:
Goal
------
Make a compact, low-operator bootstrap pattern that works for both small bare-metal racks and vSphere-managed private clusters. This is intentionally minimal: avoid introducing an operator dependency during first-boot/cluster-init so field teams can bring up Kubernetes clusters in constrained environments (limited network, single-control-plane acceptable for staging, thinlifespan worker nodes for testing).

Assumptions and constraints
---------------------------
- Target OS: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (cloud-init enabled) for baremetal images; photon/ubuntu templates for vSphere.
- Minimal internet access during bootstrap: apt proxies or internal mirrors expected.
- No cluster lifecycle operators during initial bootstrap phase. Operators can be installed by post-bootstrap reconciler when control plane is stable.
- Terraform is the source of truth for infra (PXE/DHCP records, vSphere VM templates, VLANs, load balancers).
- BMC/IPMI available for hardware in RACK sites but may be firewalled; plan for manual console fallback.

High-level sequence (operatorless)
----------------------------------
1) Provision infra via Terraform 
   - Create networks, DNS entries, LB VIP (if available).
   - Provision control-plane VMs (3 recommended for prod; single for staging).
2) Base image boot and cloud-init runs:
   - cloud-init scoped to run kubeadm preflight tasks and write join tokens to metadata server or Terraform-managed secret store.
3) Kubeadm init on primary control-plane node (explicit systemd unit, idempotent script).
4) API reachable -> create bootstrap token + CA certs persisted to Vault/secret-store.
5) Join workers via kubeadm join using token from secret-store.
6) Apply minimal static manifests (coredns, kube-proxy, local-cni) from a gated Git repo (git-sync job run manually or via short-lived script).
7) Sanity checks + smoke e2e (node ready, DNS resolution, curl to kube-apiserver).
8) Install reconcilers/operators as post-boot step (ArgoCD or Helm operator).

Operational checklist (quick)
----------------------------
- Preflight before provisioning:
  - Confirm DHCP scope and PXE server reachability (baremetal).
  - vSphere: verify VM template versions and customization spec.
  - Mirror packages for apt and container registries reachable from subnet.
  - KMS/HSM access for secrets (if private cluster uses customer keys).
- During provisioning:
  - Monitor terraform apply logs for DNS/LB resource readiness.
  - Watch cloud-init logs (/var/log/cloud-init-output.log) for early failures.
  - Collect first-boot journal on control plane if kubeadm fails.
- Post bootstrap validation:
  - kubectl get nodes (all Ready).
  - kubectl get pods -n kube-system (coredns and kube-proxy running).
  - Run a tiny DNS e2e pod (busybox nslookup).

Terraform module notes (practical)
--------------------------------
- Keep modules small and composable: network, control-plane-vm, worker-vm, dns-records, lb-vip, bmc-provision.
- Expose only necessary parameters in module interface: template_name, cpu, memory, disk_gb, network_ids, cloud-init-template (string), tags. Avoid passing large maps of internal logic.
- State handling: use a per-environment remote state (S3/GCS) with locking (DynamoDB/Cloud SQL). For air-gapped sites use an isolated S3-compatible object store.
- Secrets: do NOT put tokens/CA in terraform state. Instead write a small post-provision hook to persist cluster bootstrap secrets to Vault and write placeholder (secret path) back into the Terraform outputs.
- Idempotency: cloud-init script must be safe to re-run. Bake a sentinel under /etc/bootstrap-complete so re-runs short-circuit.

Sample terraform workflow (recommended)
------------------------------------
- terraform plan -> review in PR -> apply in CI runner with restricted credentials.
- After apply success, trigger post-provision job (ci-job or manual) that SSHs to primary control-plane and kicks off kubeadm init if cloud-init did not.

Bootstrap script (outline)
------------------------
- Step 0: Wait for package mirror reachable (retry loop).
- Step 1: Install containerd, runc, cri-tools, kubeadm/kubelet/kubectl pinned to same version.
- Step 2: sysctl net.bridge.bridge-nf-call-iptables=1, swapoff -a persist removal from /etc/fstab.
- Step 3: Run kubeadm init --config /etc/kubeadm/config.yaml --upload-certs || write failure to /var/log/bootstrap-failure.log.
- Step 4: Persist admin kubeconfig to secret-store endpoint (Vault path or S3 with restricted ACL).
- Step 5: Create small manager pod that applies static manifests from git repo (if api is ready).

Upgrade plan (control plane + workers)
------------------------------------
- Strategy: control-plane first, then workers. Prefer surge strategy on workers if cluster.autoscaler not present.
- Preconditions:
  - etcd backup + snapshot stored off-node and verified.
  - All core system pods at Ready.
  - No ongoing long-running migrations (DB jobs, kafka rolling updates).
- Steps (minor version bump example):
  1) Take etcd snapshot and verify upload success.
  2) Drain one control plane node -> apply kubeadm upgrade apply on that node -> uncordon and verify API health.
  3) Repeat control plane nodes sequentially.
  4) Upgrade kubelet on worker nodes via Terraform machine image or OSC-level package update and reboot pattern (drain/upgrade/uncordon).
- Rollback signal: if any control plane node fails to become Ready within X minutes (configurable, suggested 15m), stop and escalate to SRE-runbook. Keep last-known-good etcd snapshot to restore.

Rollback and recovery notes
--------------------------
- Fast restore path (control-plane only): 
  - Restore etcd from last-known-good snapshot to a new control-plane VM set (templated) and rejoin workers.
- Conservative path (full restore):
  - Provision new cluster (isolated network), restore etcd, reconfigure DNS/LB to point to new VIPs.
- For partial worker corruption: reprovision worker VM via Terraform (taint + apply). Keep PV reclaim policy documented; for PVs with RWX mount, avoid abrupt recreate unless application tolerates.

Testing and verification (simple checklist)
-----------------------------------------
- Unit smoke: kube-apiserver reachable, controller-manager healthy.
- Integration: deploy a small statefulset (single replica) and verify readiness, scale to 3 and verify reschedule.
- Latency sanity: curl /healthz from app-subnet and control-plane subnet, expect <50ms internal.
- Cost/size check: record flops/CPU and memory per pod to validate capacity plan.

Common failure modes & troubleshooting tips
------------------------------------------
- cloud-init failing due to apt mirror: check /var/log/cloud-init-output.log, add mirror fallback.
- kubeadm preflight fails for swap: ensure swap removed in both systemd and fstab.
- kubelet crashloop after upgrade: check containerd version mismatch; pin runtime and kubelet to compatible versions.
- DNS flaps: ensure coreDNS configmap limits and node local dns cache not introduced prematurely.

Open questions / TODOs
---------------------
- Decide default: single-control-plane vs 3-node CP for staging; lean toward single for faster rollouts but with explicit warnings.
- Automation: prototype a tiny ephemeral CI runner that can apply terraform + run kubeadm init automatically and stream logs to S3 for remote debugging.
- Vault integration: finalize secret write pattern for bootstrap tokens (path convention, rotation policy).
- Offline installer: create tarball of minimal container images required and a guide for loading into private registry during airgap provisioning.

Notes to reviewers
------------------
- This is intentionally conservative and operatorless for first-boot reliability in field sites. After the cluster is healthy we should switch to our standard reconciler model (ArgoCD) for installing operators and infra components.
- Feedback requested on the terraform secret pattern and whether we should allow terraform to create the initial kubeadm token (I prefer creating it from the control-plane to avoid token leaking into state).

Appendix: quick commands
------------------------
- Check cloud-init: journalctl -u cloud-init -b --no-pager | tail -n 200
- kubeadm init (manual): kubeadm init --config /etc/kubeadm/config.yaml --upload-certs
- snapshot etcd (etcdctl): ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot save /tmp/snap.db --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 --cacert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/ca.crt --cert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.crt --key=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.key

End of note.
